headline: State Park Day Use and Backcountry Check
reservation: Grafton Notch State Park generally operates on a first-come, first-served basis for day use. While no entry permit is required for hiking, check official Maine State Park sites for any updated parking or camping regulations in the Mahoosuc Range.

days.title: Grafton Notch Geology

stops.name: Screw Auger Falls
stops.detail: Observe the 23-foot twisting gorge and natural rock potholes carved by the Bear River.

stops.name: Moose Cave
stops.detail: Follow the interpretive loop to a slot canyon where the river disappears into a granite cavern.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; Route 26 is well-maintained but narrow.
days.note: These roadside stops are accessible to most but can be slippery during spring melt.

days.title: Rugged Ridge Hikes

stops.name: Old Speck Mountain
stops.detail: Climb Maine’s third-highest peak for 360-degree views from the summit fire tower.

stops.name: Table Rock
stops.detail: Hike to a massive granite ledge for a vertical perspective overlooking the notch.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; parking at the Appalachian Trail crossing is limited.
days.note: The terrain is exceptionally rocky; allow more time than mileage suggests for mountain safety.

days.title: Western Maine Valleys

stops.name: Step Falls Preserve
stops.detail: Walk along cascading pools and smooth granite slabs perfect for summer wading.

stops.name: Evans Notch (Route 113)
stops.detail: Drive this winding border road for views of the Baldfaces and dense forest wilderness.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours; Route 113 is seasonal and very narrow in sections.
days.note: Route 113 through Evans Notch typically closes for the winter season.

intel.title: Grafton Notch Access
intel.text: Small lots at Screw Auger Falls fill quickly during summer weekends. Arrive before 10 AM to secure a space near the primary trailheads.

intel.title: Remote Terrain
intel.text: Cell service is virtually non-existent once you leave the Route 2 corridor. Carry a physical map for navigation in the Mahoosuc Notch area.

intel.title: Gateway Provisions
intel.text: Bethel is the last reliable source for fuel and groceries before entering the state park. There are no services available once you travel north into the Notch.

intel.title: Black Fly Season
intel.text: Be prepared for heavy biting insect activity from mid-May through June. July and August offer much more comfortable conditions for high-ridge hiking.

intel.title: Road Seasonality
intel.text: The scenic Route 113 through Evans Notch is not plowed in winter. Check MaineDOT for seasonal opening dates, usually occurring in late May.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Augusta State Airport (AUG) and drive approximately 95 minutes to Bethel for local supply shopping and lodging check-in.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle is fine for paved routes, but high-clearance is better for remote logging road access.
plan.goldenHour: Table Rock offers a prime viewpoint for watching the sunset over the Mahoosuc Range, with fall being the peak season.
